newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise, eye US Treasuries, FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise, eye US Treasuries, FOMC.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose on Monday, tracking last Friday's overnight rise in U.S. Treasuries, and dealers said the market was confident a U.S. rate hike was unlikely this week.
"Trading started from firmer levels as U.S. Treasuries closed higher overnight," National Reserve Bank dealer Andrei Ivanov-Golitsyn said. "Trading has been going on in the same ranges since then."

The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee is due to meet on July 1 and 2. MinFins, along with other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news suggesting a change in U.S. interest rates and U.S. Treasury bond prices.
Dealers said the market was generally expecting the FOMC to keep the rates unchanged, with banks looking carefully for hints in the development of the U.S. economy.
"Trading activity is normal despite the summer holiday season," Imperial Bank dealer Alexei Denisov said. "We are waiting for the FOMC meeting and other important figures due this week."
U.S. June unemployment is due on Thursday.
